non_blocking_findings: THE CAP NEVER TRUNCATES, AND LOWER IS STRICTLY BETTER. Every run at 256, 512 and 2048 returned stopReason tool_use with a valid tool block: the model emits the tool call and THEN keeps writing, so output saturates at whatever cap is set and the cap simply cuts the waste. C1's 'headroom' justification for 2048 is inverted by this evidence, and the value was lowered to 512 under the blocking performance finding.

THE SUB-5-SECOND GOAL IS MET TYPICALLY BUT NOT GUARANTEED. Four post-fix samples ranged 1024-5417ms, median about 2.6 seconds, with one sample just over five. The worst case fell from 19,299ms to 5,417ms. Task 3's live check should expect a few seconds with occasional excursions, not a hard bound.

ONE SAMPLE AT CAP 256 RETURNED unsupported for a harder question at 114 output tokens - below the cap, so not truncation. It may be a legitimate refusal or model variance; 512 answered the same question with a selection, which is why 256 was not chosen.

DO NOT TRUST A SINGLE SAMPLE OF THIS MODEL: output length for the same prompt at temperature 0 ranged from 106 to 24,313 tokens across this task's measurements. The contract's original 2048 was justified on one lucky sample of 1,429ms/168 tokens, which repeated sampling showed to be unrepresentative.
D-0024 and D-0031 remain open, so every leaf was judged by its testcase name and executed count.
